source_title: Opposition Mock Parliament: Akhilesh Yadav Questions EC's Neutrality as INDIA Bloc Prepares Public Impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar
source_excerpt:
The political confrontation over alleged vote theft and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls has intensified, with the INDIA bloc preparing a symbolic mock parliament in Delhi to target Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav questioned the neutrality of the Election Commission, alleging that its functioning poses a serious threat to democracy and the Constitution. He said the mock parliament is intended to send a strong message to the government and confirmed that all INDIA bloc parties will participate in the November 1 mega rally. The public impeachment-style programme is being organised at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's residence, with former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar scheduled to preside over the proceedings. Kharge will introduce the proposal, while representatives of 19 opposition parties are expected to present their arguments. Each party representative will initially be given six minutes to speak, with additional time possible depending on parliamentary strength. Individuals who claim their names were wrongfully deleted from electoral rolls, along with civil society representatives, have also been invited to present their testimonies as evidence. Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, is scheduled to deliver the concluding speech. In a symbolic move, the government benches will remain empty, representing the opposition's allegation that the government is defending the Chief Election Commissioner without addressing its concerns. Posters describing the event as the public impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar have also been put up outside Kharge's residence. Congress leaders have alleged that they faced difficulties obtaining permission to organise the programme at other venues. With the opposition demanding accountability from the Election Commission and preparing for a massive rally at Ramlila Maidan, the political battle over electoral transparency has entered another significant phase.
